Absence of photophobia, phonophobia, vomiting, or visual disturbances — strongly argues against migraine and makes IIH less likely (as visual symptoms are nearly universal in established IIH).
No focal neurologic deficits — consistent with primary headache or functional disorder, not structural pathology.
No pulsatile tinnitus — a highly specific sign for IIH; its absence reduces likelihood.
Intermittent ibuprofen use without overuse pattern — rules out medication-overuse headache.
No personal or family history of migraine — reduces probability of vestibular migraine or chronic migraine.
All diagnostic tests (fundoscopy, MRI/MRV, TSH, orthostatics, LP) are pending — meaning no objective evidence yet supports IIH or other secondary causes.

gaps.info: Lumbar puncture opening pressure and CSF composition
gaps.discriminates: Directly confirms or excludes IIH (elevated opening pressure with normal CSF) versus normal pressure supporting primary headache/functional dizziness.
Papilledema would support IIH; its absence with normal LP would favor CTTH/functional dizziness.

gaps.info: Orthostatic vital signs (supine/standing BP and HR)
gaps.discriminates: Orthostatic intolerance/POTS would explain headache+dizziness+nausea and favor autonomic/functional etiology over CTTH.
